name: Pearl Diving

comments.body:
[b]For those playing Classic Wow: [/b]

I was able to solo this at level 32 as a warrior. 

However [i][u]my class does not matter[/u].[b][/b][/i] as I did not fight anything or use any "warrior-ish" abilities to complete the quest.

It's my opinion [i]any class[b][/b][/i] can solo this if [i]patient[/i] enough and willing to take a few extra minutes to carefully scope things out before you dive every-time you see a clam.

You may (do) want a water breathing potion with you. (I didn't have one and it likely took me a lot of extra time having to resurface for air after every single dive down)

[b]The Details[/b]:

What you need to do (besides keep a careful eye out for murloc elites and hopefully (do) bring a breathing potion, is stay away from the main concentration of murlocs.  ie: The underwater city /ruins. 

How?

If you have a quest helper addon, (cheater) stay to the farthest "outer rim" or edge of where it shows the quest location area. 

If you don't have an addon (and many on Classic wont because Classic players never cheat...) swim out as far as you can from the murloc populated ruins [i][b]while still being able to spot clams in the water below you.[/b]
[/i]

[b]Recap[i][/i][/b]:

You need to swim out as far away from those murloc infested ruins as you are able to go [i]where clams still spawn and murloc elites are far more scarce) 
[b][/b][/i]

This is where some of that patented Classic Wow patience (and of course non-cheating) will come in handy.

You'll almost certainly [i]need[b][/b][/i] to be patient to spot the clams. Not only that but patience to spot clams away from those murloc badies waiting to ruin your day. 

For me, I panned the camera angle directly down into the water from above my toon's head, but you should do it whatever way is best for you.

Some clams are hidden by the terrain and / or even almost completely "buried" in the surrounding scenery. 

For me, mousing over the areas I was checking was a huge help (You'll see your cursor become a gear wheel when you mouse over a clam)  

Be sure there are no murlocs too close to where you dive or they will attack you. 

I was spotted by one of the elite murlocs and attacked only once but I was fortunately able to swim away before I was rendered into warrior pate' 

[b](You can also skip all of the above if you have the gold. Check the auction house as they are able to be farmed and sold there as well)[i][u][/u][/i][/b]

Happy pearl hunting. 

[small]Disclaimer

I personally don't think anyone is cheating when using (most) addons in Classic Wow. 

Merely jesting.

No elite murlocs (or low level warriors) were harmed in the making of this post[/small]
If you are an engineer he will offer you the Schematic for the flash bomb aswell
Its at the Vile Reef and you find them in giant clams around 25:23. They are located in a large area and there are loads of Murlocsl. The murlocs are lvl35-36 elites and gives nice xp.

This quest can be done at the same time as the Encrusted Fins quest, recieved in Shimmering Flats. Every clam had a pearl in it, and every Murloc dropped a Fin as well. Make sure to have some waterbreathing buff, however. 

If you swim what looks like a few "meters" below the surface (inches on your screen) around the outside edge of the dark area on the map that is Vile Reef, you should be able to see the clams clearly when looking down. They are located near rocks or at the base of large tree-like kelpweed areas on the sides of the reef valley.Murlocs guard about half of the clams, and can be tough (at least for my clothie mage), and they like to run when they get low on health so save your nuke weapon or spell for that. 

Sorry, I don't use coordinates, but Vile Reef is located off-shore, directly west of the Horde Grom'Gol Base Camp on the western shore of Stranglethorn. Both quests can be done here.

Here's a tip for everyone, there is an item that drops in Gnomeregan calle Hydrocane, it drops off a boss that's fairly early on and fairly easy to defeat if you just grab a couple friends.  Hydrocane has only the requirement of being able to use staves, which is much easier then the engineering helm, which is a pain in the butt to build up to, and allows you to breathe underwater.  I'm a 47 hunter, got it by the fact that no one else wanted it, and use it for stuff like this and underwater mining since I mostly just use my gun if I run into something.

If you can re-set the video options for high-detail, you can see the clamshells a little easier. Everyone is right that you can avoid the elite murlocs and you should because they have three annoying traits. 

1) Almost all of them are paired or tripled, but the second one is hidden, stealthed or behind some seaweed. Combine that with an odd patrol pattern and a long aggro range and it's hard to fight just one, so be prepared. 2) Although most don't hit very hard (lots of hit points, though), some of the Saltscale Foragers have some kind of random spell. One killed my 39 Voidwalker in 2 hits (twinked murlocs?) and another killed a 41 shielded priest at nearly full health in about 3 blows. Boy, was she surprised, and not very happy because these are 36-38 elites. Weird. 3) Of course everyone tries to pull them from their pals, which is a good tactic, particularly if you can keep hitting them but be careful, if you lose the pull and they stop or start to turn back, they will jump back to full health immediately. Very annoying if you've spent five minutes hammering away on one. Even more annoying when you work hard to kill one for a long battle and he drops 83 copper. I can hear the designers' sarcastic laughter now.

The clams don't respawn very quickly, so for best results (the most amount of clams), go in the early morning or late at night, server time. Otherwise it will take you 45 minutes to an hour to find nine. The rewards aren't much (unless you're an engineer) but the XP is great and the Vile Reef is scenic.

I started this quest and as soon as I started fighting the murlocs I would have to swim back to the surface. I drowned a lot. Here's what you do. Get close enough the murlocs to agro them, then simply swim back to the surface, with murloc trailing behind you. Once you are safely breathing the cool ocean air, you are then free to kill murloc. Once murloc is dead then swim down to get the clams. You may have to do this a few times(depending on the amount of murlocs). I hope this helps you.

Quick tip: If you have less that 3/4 breath when diving, forget about it as this is a struggle at certain depths to get back up on time, then energy drained form me at a rate of 415hp every 2 seconds while I was out of breath!

I went by a number of the coordinates listed here and despite their well-intentioned recording the quest is still a hide-and-seek.  The coordinates each cover an area which, while totally visible on land, is mired with plants, rocks, hills, and reefs undersea.  Put it this way - if you like Easter Egg hunts, you'll love this.

The good news is that I counted at least 15 separate clam locations, so you are very likely to bump into 9 of them.  The general areas indicated by the coords are the most fruitful.

About the coords. I mean, the clams are like... Everywhere. And you don't have to kill the murlocs either if you don't feel to.
